# Pārivāsikakkhandhaka (Kd 12)

**ID:** Kd 12  
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Pārivāsikakkhandhaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pārivāsikakkhandhaka* is the twelfth chapter of the Khandhaka section of the Vinaya Piṭaka, located in the *Cullavagga* immediately after the *Kammakkhandhaka* and before the *Samuccayakkhandhaka* [Norman 1983; Frauwallner 1956; Banerjee 1979]. It contains a detailed treatment of the conduct and duties required of a monastic who has committed an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), outlining the standards of behavior to be observed while undergoing probation (*parivāsa*) in order to qualify for rehabilitation, as well as the conditions under which probation may temporarily be kept under suspension [Banerjee 1979]. In English, the chapter has been translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In comparative analysis, A. C. Banerjee notes that the Tibetan version largely corresponds with the Pali concerning the duties of a monk on probation and the suspension of probation, though unlike the Pali version it opens with an introductory narrative [Banerjee 1979].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd13 Pudgalavastu; xct-mu-kd13 Parivāsa; lzh-mu-kd13 Parivāsa; Lzh Sarv Kd12b b. Parivāsa Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 13 Parivāsa Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 16 Parivāsa Khandhaka
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn2 Vagga 2. Ukkhepanīya; san-mu-kd12 Pudgalavastu; xct-mu-kd12 Samuccaya; lzh-mu-kd12 Samuccaya; Lzh Sarv Kd12a a. Samuccaya Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 12 Samuccaya Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 10a a. Samuccaya Khandhaka; Kd 13 Samuccayakkhandhaka; Kd 9 Campeyyakkhandhaka

**Sources**

- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (1983) — Gave the translation title 'Probation' and confirmed sequence within the Khandhaka collection.
- [Frauwallner 1956] Erich Frauwallner, The Earliest Vinaya and the Beginnings of Buddhist Literature (1956) — Documented canonical sequence of chapters in the Cullavagga.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvāstivāda Literature (1979) — Described parivāsa regulations, relative placement after Kammakkhandhaka, and comparison with the Tibetan version.
